_comment: SHOSMED physics, THIRD 60-question block. Implemented 19 November 2026 from
SHOSMED_Physics_Batch3_Review_and_Claude_Prompt.txt.
HOW THE IDS WERE VERIFIED. The review supplied ORIGINAL IDENTIFICATION
SIGNATURES and explicitly warned against assuming phys-121..phys-180,
contiguity or zero overlap, so the map was derived by FULL CONTENT MATCH of
each original stem plus all four original option texts against all 280
physics records, on a canonical form that decodes named HTML entities,
strips tags, folds sub/superscripts to plain digits and normalises dashes,
Greek letters, arrows and whitespace.
- All 60 matched EXACTLY, with no need for the whitespace-insensitive
fallback the previous block required.
- No two of the 280 records share a signature under either form, so no
match was ambiguous and none needed the explanation as a tie-break.
- Every stored topic equalled the signature topic.
- All 60 stored answer letters equalled the review key block, and the
review changes no letter, so NO key was changed and there is no
disagreement to report. The tally stays A=8, B=29, C=21, D=2.
The block turns out to be phys-121 .. phys-180 in display order, contiguous,
but that is a RESULT of the matching rather than the assumption the review
warned against. It does not overlap the 120 ids of the two earlier blocks
(phys-1..phys-120), so all 60 are newly reviewed ids.
THE Q56 MAPPING CAUTION. The review warns that its Q56 shares the area and
speed data of the previous block's Q41 but has a different option set and
answer position. Matched on the full signature, this Q56 is phys-176 and the
previous block's Q41 is phys-101: different records. phys-101 was not touched
in this pass.
DISTRACTOR FEEDBACK AS STORED, inspected rather than assumed:
- Q1..Q55 carried NO distractor feedback of any kind: no feedback heading
in any form and no lettered feedback paragraph. The 165 bodies added
there duplicate nothing.

- Q56..Q60 each carried three bodies, stored as a

block
at the end of the main explanation, with option-text lead-ins and no
option letters. Each of those five blocks was reconstructed byte for byte
from the spec before being touched. The seven bodies the review retains
are carried over verbatim, markup included, and only the eight it names
were replaced. The <ul> list becomes one paragraph per incorrect option,
which is the form the review asks for and the form the rest of the bank
uses.
- Feedback is placed after the main explanation and before the Key Concept,
as the review directs, under the bank's <h4>Why the other choices are
wrong: heading. Each heading is derived from that item's own stored
option text, so a renamed option carries its new text into its heading.
STRUCTURE AS STORED, checked rather than assumed: this block has NO tables,
no Key Educational Points block and no Bottom Line, and every item has
exactly one Key Concept and an unlettered keyed heading that reproduces its
keyed option. Two structural details differ from the plain-text export and
are recorded under 'deviations': Q17 stores an empty styled <div> after its
Key Concept, and Q56..Q59 store an 'exp-diagram' <div> holding the worked
formula inside the main explanation.
NOTATION. Q47 stores A₀/2<sup>n</sup>, Q52 stores (1/2)<sup>n</sup> and
Q53 stores <sup>235</sup><sub>92</sub>U etc. All three are already correct
markup that the plain-text export flattened, so none was changed, exactly as
the review's instruction 7 requires. The one genuine stored notation defect
is Q48, whose options and explanation used the UPPERCASE Greek letters
U+0391, U+0392 and U+0393 for the particle symbols; the review's own option
replacements put α, β and γ in their place and its replacement
explanation and Key Concept remove the uppercase forms from the prose.

deviations:
Q17 stores an EMPTY styled div,
, after its Key Concept. It holds no content and is invisible apart from a 12px gap. The review's inventory names no change to it and instruction 6 says to report rather than delete what the export did not show, so it was left exactly as stored and is reported here.

Q56, Q58 and Q59 keep an 'exp-diagram' div holding their worked formula, because the review retains their main explanations. Q57's main explanation is one of the 20 replaced, and the review's replacement prose carries its formula inline, so that item's exp-diagram div is gone. Divs in the block therefore go from 5 to 4. No div was added.

The existing Q56..Q60 feedback was stored as a <ul> of three <li> items with option-text lead-ins, not as paragraphs. Converting it to one paragraph per incorrect option with the option letters added is what the review's instruction 4 asks for, so the five <ul> lists and their 15 <li> items are gone from the block.
notes: The review's own inventory was cross-checked and closes: the displays touched by a stem, main-explanation, Key Concept or option change leave exactly the thirteen the review lists as core-content-kept (Q1, Q4, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q11, Q12, Q15, Q22, Q27, Q29, Q45, Q49), and the items whose only existing-content change is the Key Concept are exactly Q14, Q53 and Q55.

No answer letter, id, topic or subject moved, and no answer-position rebalancing was done. Q19 B, Q39 C and Q48 A/B/C are text replacements in place; Q19's, Q39's and Q48's keyed headings are re-synchronized to the renamed keyed option.
'Back to Dashboard', 'Unanswered' and 'Report an issue' appear in no stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so they are interface text and are not counted as content corrections.
No CSS was changed. The approved review-option wrappers and the scoped sup/sub rule are untouched, and no bank-wide Unicode normalization was applied.
Structural and consistency checks establish scope and presentation. They do not establish scientific accuracy, which rests on the content review itself.
